nodes.label: ADR 001 — Parent workspace as SDK YAML; domain workspaces derived as JSON
nodes.norm_label: adr 001 — parent workspace as sdk yaml; domain workspaces derived as json
nodes.rationale: Accepted. The repo, not the live org, must be the source of truth so a cold rebuild into a fresh org is possible and children are diffable review artifacts. Parent stored as gooddata-python-sdk declarative YAML (one file per object, store_declarative_workspace), never authored in the UI. 12 domain workspaces are never authored — derived by a splitter driven by an explicit domains.yaml manifest into generated/workspaces/globalmart-<domain>.json and published from there; each child gets an LDM pruned to datasets reachable from its retained metrics/visualizations. Rejected: export-live-parent-to-JSON (live org becomes truth, 2.9 MB unreviewable diffs, non-reproducible LLM descriptions), UI-authoring hybrid with pull-back (extra step that gets skipped, round-trip fidelity unproven), id-prefix domain membership (mixed-domain dashboards silently dropped), full LDM copied into every child (all 225 datasets exposed, distorts AI search/routing evaluation). Trade-offs: loses UI authoring — adding a dashboard means editing YAML; splitter and pruner become load-bearing code needing tests; domains.yaml must be maintained. Existing transitive MAQL-closure split logic in publish_domain_workspaces.py is hardened, not discarded. Revisit if YAML authoring is too slow for the content-change rate — then add a proven round-trip so UI edits can be pulled back safely.

nodes.label: ADR 002 — Publishing requires an explicit --apply
nodes.rationale: Accepted. Every command that writes to a live GoodData org is a read-only rehearsal by default and writes only with --apply. The rehearsal runs the whole pipeline (preflight, datasource resolution, placeholder substitution, assert_fully_resolved, backup, diff) and stops at the three write calls; a backup of the target's current layout is taken immediately before the PUT, and --no-backup is refused without --apply. WHY: put_declarative_workspace has REPLACE semantics — it overwrites a workspace's entire content in one call; targets are real (petertomko.demo.cloud, the local-inference host) and API tokens are often scoped more broadly than the workspace; a mistyped profile with a write-by-default CLI silently destroys a layout that exists nowhere else. Mirrors terraform plan/apply, which the user already works in. Rejected: write-by-default + --dry-run (the dangerous path is the accidental one; rated High/High in the spec risk table), interactive confirmation (breaks CI and agents, gets muscle-memoried away), automatic backup only (recovery, not prevention; restoring 2.9 MB into a live org is itself risky). Trade-offs: every real publish is two commands; docs and CI must carry --apply; a test must pin the default. Rehearsal still reads from the host, so it is not offline and still needs credentials. Revisit only by adding a per-profile require_apply:false opt-out in config/targets.yaml for throwaway orgs, never by flipping the global default.

nodes.label: ADR 003 — What under generated/ is committed, and what is regenerated
nodes.norm_label: adr 003 — what under generated/ is committed, and what is regenerated
nodes.rationale: Accepted; clarifies ADR 001. The rule in one line: commit what a human reviews, regenerate what a machine consumes. generated/workspaces/*.json (the 12 derived domain layouts) is committed because a diff there says 'this metric left the HR child' — exactly the review surface ADR 001 exists to produce. Warehouse rows are never committed: hundreds of MB of CSV with no meaningful git delta would make the repo unusable within a few iterations. Committed for data instead: the DDL and data/archive-manifest.json pinning archive version, URL, sha256, per-table row counts and checksums — a sharper review surface than a CSV diff nobody reads. Amended 2026-09-18: the generator was descoped to FEAT-007, so data is fetched and verified against a committed manifest rather than regenerated from a recorded seed; the reviewability split is unchanged, only the recovery mechanism differs, and the local cache .cache/globalmart-data/ is gitignored as generated/data/** was. Rejected: commit everything (~900 MB per scale, unusable history, review noise), commit nothing (loses ADR 001's point — silent split regressions return), Git LFS / object storage (reintroduces the external dependency goal-01 exists to remove — the S3 bucket problem renamed). Trade-off: one directory carries two .gitignore rules, which looks inconsistent without this ADR.

nodes.label: ADR 004 — Warehouse loads substitute a census and refusal guards for ADR 002's backup
nodes.norm_label: adr 004 — warehouse loads substitute a census and refusal guards for adr 002's backup
nodes.rationale: Accepted; a stated, bounded deviation from ADR 002. ADR 002's backup-before-destructive-call holds for workspace layouts (a few MB; backup_workspace() writes a directly republishable tree) but not for warehouse loads, which truncate and repopulate 215 tables (~900 MB at scale 1.0) — copying that before every load is impractical and the copy would be no more valuable than the seed that produced it. Substituted: (1) a pre-load census — row counts plus per-table checksum of the target schema recorded in the run report before any truncation, for forensics; (2) two refusal guards — the target profile must declare data_owned:true and the target schema must contain only tables the generator's registry knows, so a load cannot stomp a warehouse this repo does not own; (3) --apply still gates the write, unchanged. Stated honestly: the census is prevention and forensics, not a restore path — the restore path is regenerating from the recorded seed and scale, acceptable for generated data and not for hand-authored content, which is why the deviation is scoped to the loader alone. Rejected: full data backup per load (~900 MB copied, would discourage running loads), warehouse-native snapshot/time travel (MotherDuck and Postgres differ; couples the repo to warehouse features), --apply with no guard (a mistyped schema silently destroys a warehouse). The data_owned flag is load-bearing, not decorative. Revisit if a target ever holds rows this repo did not generate.
